To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel low cost and distributed embedded system for structural health monitoring of critical buildings, using very cost effective MEMs accelerometers.

we have developed a distributed embedded system for structural health monitoring that uses very cost-effective MEMS accelerometers instead of more expensive transducers, and we have developed a low cost and synchronized devices that allow a comprehensive assessment of a whole building, by using the response to vibrations of the different sensors.

we have developed a low cost, distributed, embedded platform for SHM of critical buildings, based on MEMS accelerometers and a STM32 microcontroller, with a WiFi transceiver, that performs a digital filter and fusion of the data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an innovative low cost SHM system for critical structures, based on the fusion of the measurements collected from MEMS accelerometers.
the design and implementation of an embedded system for Structural health monitoring (SHM) of critical buildings.

1) a new method for the design and calibration of a MEMS-based distributed SHM system; 2) a low cost and low power embedded system for online filtering and fusion; 3) the use of a WiFi transceiver to transmit data after elaboration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system proposed in this paper is a very cost effective, low power and distributed embedded platform for structural health monitoring.
our work poses the basis to develop low cost methods for monitoring the structural health of buildings and civil structures.
we have developed a low cost, distributed, and wireless embedded system for SHM that is able to process data directly on board and to transmit them after filtering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that a distributed low cost SHM system is possible, by exploiting a low cost microprocessor and low cost sensors.
the presented system is a distributed low cost platform for structural health monitoring of critical infrastructures, such as buildings, bridges and tunnels.
we have developed a low cost and distributed SHM platform that can provide a more accurate evaluation of the state of the building.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed system is able to provide a reliable and cost effective solution for monitoring the structural health of critical buildings, such as hospitals, schools, museums and so on.
the low cost MEMS accelerometers are able to detect the main vibration modes of a building and to provide a reliable estimate of the vibration level.
MEMS sensors can be used in SHM, and that the proposed architecture can be used for low cost monitoring of buildings and infrastructures.
